1.explanation:
• BpmnImporter.prototype.add (lib/import/BpmnImporter.js) is responsible for creating connection elements and (conditionally) their external labels. Currently it only calls addLabel if getLabel(element) returns a truthy label, which does not pick up Message Flow “name” properties. To display message names here, addLabel must be invoked unconditionally for bpmn:MessageFlow even when no DI label bounds exist, or getLabel must be extended to read semantic.name.  

• LabelUtil.isLabelExternal (lib/util/LabelUtil.js) flags MessageFlow as an element that should receive an external label. It works correctly, but downstream code never honors its result for message flows.  

• LabelUtil.getExternalLabelBounds (lib/util/LabelUtil.js) computes where to place an external label on a flow. It must be exercised for MessageFlow; message-specific offset logic might need adjustment so the name doesn’t overlap the envelope icon.  

• BpmnRenderer.prototype.drawConnection (lib/draw/BpmnRenderer.js) draws the dashed line and message icon but does not render the label shape created by the importer. The renderer must be updated to discover and render label shapes for connection elements (e.g. by delegating to textRenderer for child label shapes).  

Together, these classes/functions form the import→layout→render pipeline for external labels on message flows; they must be extended or fixed to pick up BPMN messageFlow.name, create the label shape at the correct position, and draw it under the envelope icon.
1.bug_scenario: In the provided BPMN diagram many of the Message Flow connections (dashed lines with envelope icons) carry a “name” in the underlying BPMN XML but no text label is ever rendered under the envelope. The red-boxed Message Flow (and many like it) show only an envelope icon on a dashed line with no “message name” text, even though the BPMN data for those flows has a <messageFlow name=“…”> set.

2.bug_scenario: In the provided BPMN diagram message flows display the little envelope icon in the middle of the dashed connection but never show the actual name of the underlying <bpmn:Message> (or the name carried on the MessageFlow). In other words, although LabelUtil marks MessageFlows as “external labels,” and the importer even tries to create a label if getLabel(element) returns text, no text ever appears with the envelope icon. The red‐boxed example in the lower lane highlights exactly one of these nameless message icons.
